name: National pension fund investment manager (single global fund, mostly internal management)
modelled_on: A large Canadian national public pension fund manager (name withheld), public information for fiscal years 2020 to 2022
summary: This organisation invests one national public pension fund, worth about C$539 billion at March 31, 2022, on behalf of the contributors and beneficiaries of a national pension plan. It does not sell products: its income is the investment return on the fund, and its single objective set in law is to maximise returns without undue risk of loss, while its own operating costs of about C$1.4 billion a year are paid out of the fund. About 2,050 employees work from a Toronto head office and eight offices in London, Luxembourg, Hong Kong, Mumbai, Sydney, New York, San Francisco and Sao Paulo. Six investment departments do the investing: Total Fund Management designs the portfolio and manages exposures, leverage and liquidity; Capital Markets and Factor Investing runs public market strategies, external managers, funding and the central trading desk; and Active Equities, Credit Investments, Private Equity and Real Assets invest in public and private companies, loans, real estate, infrastructure and energy, mostly with internal teams and alongside partners. Corporate functions under the Chief Financial and Risk Officer, General Counsel, Chief Technology and Data Officer and Chief Talent Officer, plus an investment operations group, process trades and private cash flows, value holdings, report results and oversee risk. An independent Board of Directors governs the organisation and it reports to the federal and provincial finance ministers who act as stewards.

process_map.name: Review Reference Portfolios and risk appetite
process_map.description: Portfolio design staff model the plan's assets and liabilities using the Chief Actuary's report, test candidate equity-bond mixes and recommend the Reference Portfolios and targeted market risk. The CIO, CFRO and CEO review the proposal before the Board decides. The work is slow because it combines actuarial projections, long-horizon return assumptions and stress results.
process_map.unit_of_work: one Reference Portfolio and risk appetite review

evidence.note: Legal objective of maximum return without undue risk of loss (the fund's governing act s. 5); Portfolio Design runs asset-liability modelling for periodic reviews of the Board-approved Reference Portfolios; risk appetite reviewed annually.

process_map.name: Design the Strategic Portfolio and annual target exposures
process_map.description: Each year TFM translates the Reference Portfolio and risk appetite into Strategic Portfolio weights for six asset classes and regions five years out, plus current-year target exposures. Departments and Risk give input on opportunity sets. Agreement across departments with competing ambitions makes it iterative.

evidence.note: Strategic Portfolios and TFM's annual portfolio design process described in F2021 and F2022 reports.

process_map.name: Allocate capital and set program mandates and deployment guidance
process_map.description: TFM sets each active program's target size, factor and regional characteristics and deployment range, and the CIO approves written program mandates. Guidance is refreshed quarterly as markets and pipelines change. Department heads negotiate allocations, so the work needs several rounds.

evidence.note: Active Portfolio Management guidance to 20 investment programs and CIO-approved program mandates (F2021).

process_map.name: Rebalance the Balancing Portfolio to target exposures
process_map.description: Every trading day the balancing team compares total fund exposures from the daily valuation with targets and decides when and how far to rebalance. It builds a trade list of futures, ETFs, swaps and cash securities and sends it to the central trading desk, and sends credit adjustments to Public Credit. Large private fundings and market moves force unplanned rebalancing.

evidence.note: Balancing Portfolio Management determines when, to what extent and by what means rebalancing is required (F2021).

process_map.name: Manage foreign currency exposure and hedges
process_map.description: TFM sets the fund's overall foreign currency exposure and reviews hedge ratios weekly against target, then sends FX forward and swap orders to the trading desk. Hedges must roll before expiry and their cash settlement affects liquidity. Emerging market currencies are costly to hedge.

evidence.note: TFM guides overall foreign currency exposure; hedging costs discussed in F2022.

process_map.name: Manage leverage and the funding plan
process_map.description: Each month TFM reviews recourse leverage against the Board limit and sets the mix of term debt, commercial paper, repo and synthetic financing for the funding team. The CIO approves the plan with Risk input. The trade-off between cost, tenor and liquidity under stress makes it judgment heavy.
process_map.unit_of_work: one monthly leverage and funding review

evidence.note: Recourse leverage C$122 billion in F2022 against a 45% Board limit from April 2022; borrowed funds include term debt, commercial paper and secured borrowing.

process_map.name: Forecast liquidity and monitor the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio
process_map.description: The liquidity team builds a daily cash forecast from capital calls, closings, distributions, margin, plan transfers and maturing debt, and computes the 10-day liquidity coverage ratio. It flags shortfalls to rebalancing and funding and reports the ratio to Risk. Forecasts depend on uncertain private fund call timing.

evidence.note: 10-day Liquidity Coverage Ratio of 2.9x at March 31, 2022 against a 1.0x minimum; liquidity 23% of net assets versus a 22% target.

process_map.name: Process margin calls and manage collateral
process_map.description: Collateral staff agree daily exposure with each derivative, repo and clearing counterparty, check incoming margin calls, issue calls where the fund is owed, and instruct collateral through the custodian. Disputes are escalated, and the liquidity team receives a daily margin summary. Volumes spike in volatile markets.

evidence.note: Margin disputes and collateral discrepancies are part of the cash, collateral and settlements role; margin rules for uncleared derivatives from BCBS-IOSCO.

process_map.name: Receive plan transfers and return funds for benefits
process_map.description: Each week the fund receives plan contributions not needed to pay benefits and, when needed, returns funds for benefit payments. Liquidity and accounting staff agree amounts with the plan administration, record the cash and update the forecast. Base and additional plan accounts are tracked separately.

evidence.note: Net transfers from the plan of C$8 billion in F2022 (net assets rose C$42 billion: C$34 billion income and C$8 billion transfers). The F2022 annual report (note 18.1) says amounts are transferred to the fund weekly and returned for benefits at least monthly, so about five transfers a month.

process_map.name: Issue term debt under the global debt issuance programme
process_map.description: The funding team picks currency, tenor and timing, mandates dealers, and issues bonds through the model fund Capital with a model fund guarantee, including green bonds. Legal, tax, investor relations and accounting take part. Each issue needs documentation and market windows.

evidence.note: 49 bonds totalling about C$60 billion since 2015 under a C$50 billion multi-currency programme.

process_map.name: Run commercial paper, repo and other short-term funding
process_map.description: Funding staff issue commercial paper and arrange repo and secured financing each day to meet the funding plan and liquidity forecast. Trades are booked into the investment book of record for settlement. Rolling maturities daily leaves little room for errors.

evidence.note: FCT executes financing activities and sources liquidity with secured financing (F2021); commercial paper and secured borrowing listed in F2022.

process_map.name: Research companies and make active equity portfolio decisions
process_map.description: Analysts and portfolio managers research companies, meet management, model earnings and propose buys, sells and position changes for concentrated long-short portfolios. Decisions pass through portfolio construction to remove unwanted factor exposure before orders go to trading. Getting conviction while controlling factor risk is the hard part.
process_map.unit_of_work: one portfolio decision (new position, add, trim or exit)

evidence.note: AE strategy and portfolio optimisation described in F2022; decision volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Run systematic and discretionary capital markets strategies
process_map.description: Quantitative and macro teams run models and research each day, produce target portfolios and send portfolio decisions to the trading desk. Researchers maintain models, data and backtests. Data errors and model drift are the main risks.

evidence.note: Quantitative Strategies and Risk Premia, Macro Strategies and Research and Innovation groups (F2021); strategy count is an estimate.

process_map.name: Make public credit decisions and execute credit trades
process_map.description: Public credit managers manage liquid credit and the balancing credit portfolio, decide trades and execute them with dealers, then pass fills to trade support for booking. They also execute public trades for other CI strategies. Bond liquidity varies and pricing is dealer-quoted.

evidence.note: Public Credit manages the balancing credit portfolio and executes public trades for all CI strategies (F2021).

process_map.name: Capture orders and run pre-trade compliance checks
process_map.description: Portfolio managers and the balancing team enter orders in the order management system, which checks restricted lists, limits and mandate rules. Traders accept the order and plan execution. Failed checks go back to the portfolio manager or Compliance.

evidence.note: FCT oversees global trading of all public assets except credit for all teams and the Balancing Portfolio (F2021); order volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Execute public market orders through brokers and venues
process_map.description: Central traders choose brokers, algorithms and venues, work orders across time zones and report fills. They manage market impact on large balancing trades and check execution against benchmarks. Global coverage and many order types make it demanding.

evidence.note: Centralised execution of all public assets excluding credit by FCT (F2021); volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Book, allocate and enrich executed trades
process_map.description: Trade support captures executions in the investment book of record, allocates them across portfolios and accounts, and adds settlement details from reference data. Breaks between the order system and the book of record are fixed the same day. Manual re-keying for unusual instruments causes errors.

evidence.note: Middle office trade capture and SimCorp use in the model fund postings and the SimCorp release; volume is an estimate.

process_map.name: Confirm and affirm trades with brokers and counterparties
process_map.description: Staff match allocations with brokers on the central matching platform and confirm OTC trades with counterparties, chasing unmatched trades before the market deadline. Matched trades are released for settlement. Late or wrong broker details cause most exceptions.

evidence.note: CTM matching and NI 24-101 institutional trade matching; affirmation and confirmation described in the model fund postings.

process_map.name: Instruct and settle trades with the custodian
process_map.description: Settlement staff send instructions to the custodian over SWIFT, monitor pending trades, and resolve fails with brokers and the custodian before the T+2 deadline. Failed trades are reported and cash positions updated. Cross-market holidays and missing instructions cause fails.

evidence.note: Settlement duties in the model fund posting; T+2 cycle in Canada and the U.S. from September 2017.

process_map.name: Reconcile positions and cash with custodians and brokers
process_map.description: Each day reconciliation staff compare the book of record with custodian and prime broker statements, investigate breaks and fix the side that is wrong. Clean positions go to accounting, pricing and liquidity. Timing differences and corporate actions cause many breaks.

evidence.note: Reconciliation breaks named in a model fund posting; break count is an estimate of about 15% of positions breaking at least once a month.

process_map.name: Process corporate actions and income
process_map.description: Asset servicing staff capture custodian and vendor notices, calculate entitlements, collect elections from portfolio managers for voluntary events, instruct the custodian and record income. Missed elections cost money. Events in many markets have different rules.
process_map.unit_of_work: one corporate action event per holding

evidence.note: Asset servicing named in the model fund postings; volume estimated from about 18,000 positions with two to four income events a year.

process_map.name: Account for investment transactions and income daily
process_map.description: Fund accountants review daily postings from the investment book of record, private cash flows, fees, collateral and plan transfers, clear suspense items and approve the daily ledger. Investment holding subsidiaries are not consolidated: the fund is an investment entity under IFRS 10 and carries them at fair value. Late private transaction data creates manual journals.
process_map.unit_of_work: one business day's investment accounting cycle

evidence.note: SimCorp Dimension used for portfolio accounting; consolidated statements include investment holding subsidiaries.

process_map.name: Price securities and produce the daily fund valuation
process_map.description: Pricing staff load vendor prices, check stale and outlier prices, apply fair value rules and produce the daily valuation of public holdings with the latest private values. TFM and Risk use the result for exposures the next morning. Illiquid bonds and derivatives need challenge.

evidence.note: Total funds valued at least monthly under GIPS; daily exposure management by TFM implies daily valuation.

process_map.name: Vote proxies and engage with listed companies
process_map.description: The Sustainable Investing group reviews the outside advisor's customised recommendations against the voting guidelines, decides contentious votes with portfolio managers and casts votes. It engages companies on governance and climate. Peak season from April to June compresses the work.

evidence.note: 3,817 meetings and 41,288 agenda items voted in the year to June 30, 2022; outside advisor makes customised recommendations.

process_map.name: Onboard trading counterparties and negotiate trading agreements
process_map.description: Legal negotiates ISDA master agreements, credit support annexes, repo and lending agreements, while Risk approves credit limits and Compliance completes know-your-counterparty checks. Settlement instructions are set up in reference data. Negotiation over collateral terms can take months.

evidence.note: Estimate; trading agreements are standard for derivative users subject to margin rules.

process_map.name: Source and screen direct private equity opportunities
process_map.description: Deal teams in North America, Europe and Asia receive sale processes and partner deals, check fit with the program mandate and write short screening memos. Most opportunities are declined early. Relationships with fund partners bring co-control and minority deals.

evidence.note: DPE invests alongside aligned partners (F2021); funnel shares from Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov.

process_map.name: Conduct due diligence on direct private equity investments
process_map.description: The deal team models the business, reviews the data room, hires advisors for commercial, financial, legal and environmental work, and gets tax, ESG and value creation input. It writes the investment memo for risk review and committee approval. Competitive auctions compress timelines.

evidence.note: 23.7 of 100 opportunities reach deep due diligence in the Gompers, Kaplan and Mukharlyamov survey; PVC assists in due diligence (F2021).

process_map.name: Source and screen real estate, infrastructure and energy opportunities
process_map.description: Real asset teams source assets and platforms through partners, auctions and existing portfolio companies, and screen them for mandate fit, partner quality and returns. Most real estate is done with joint venture partners. Screening memos go to deep diligence.

evidence.note: Real Estate invests mostly through joint ventures; Infrastructure invests with like-minded partners (F2021).

process_map.name: Conduct due diligence on real estate, infrastructure and energy investments
process_map.description: Deal teams review technical, regulatory, environmental and partner diligence, model long-term cash flows and agree governance rights. Tax, ESG and climate scenario input is required. The memo goes to risk review and committee approval.

evidence.note: Climate Change Security Selection Framework required where material (F2022); volume from the deal funnel.

process_map.name: Originate and screen private credit opportunities
process_map.description: Credit teams source loans, structured credit and real asset financings from sponsors, banks and platforms such as Antares Capital and screen them against the mandate. Screening memos go to underwriting. Sponsors expect quick answers.

evidence.note: CI sources direct credit through acquisitions, refinancings and platforms (F2021).

process_map.name: Underwrite private credit investments
process_map.description: The team underwrites borrower credit, collateral and structure, negotiates terms and covenants, and writes a credit memo with tax and ESG input for risk review and approval. Bespoke structures raise legal and operational risk.

evidence.note: F2022 notes operational risk from lack of standardisation in private credit processing and legal risk from bespoke transactions.

process_map.name: Source and diligence relationship and pre-IPO equity investments
process_map.description: Relationship investment and Latin America teams source significant minority stakes and pre-IPO placements, diligence the company and governance, and write the investment memo. Timing is tied to market windows and company transactions.

evidence.note: Relationship Investments and DEILA strategies (F2021); volume estimated.

process_map.name: Structure and review tax for investment transactions
process_map.description: Tax staff design holding structures, assess withholding and local taxes, review advisor opinions and sign off the tax section of investment memos and documents. Each country has different treaty rules. Late changes to deal structure force rework.

evidence.note: Tax group supports tax compliance across investment activities; taxes C$292 million in F2022.

process_map.name: Assess sustainability and climate factors in investment decisions
process_map.description: Sustainable Investing specialists review material ESG and climate risks for proposed investments, apply the climate security selection framework where material, and add findings to the memo. They also advise during ownership.

evidence.note: SI group partners with investment teams across the investment life cycle; climate framework applies where material.

process_map.name: Give an independent risk view on proposed transactions
process_map.description: Risk staff review the memo for market, credit, liquidity and concentration effects on the total fund and write a risk opinion for the committee. Short deal timetables limit review time.

evidence.note: ISRC subcommittees must consider formal guidance from accountable functions; Risk independently challenges the first line.

process_map.name: Approve investments and dispositions at the Portfolio Execution Committee
process_map.description: The Portfolio Execution Committee, chaired by the CIO, reviews memos for new investments, follow-ons, fund commitments, manager engagements and dispositions within Investment Management Authorities, with risk opinions. It approves, declines or asks for changes; large items go to the Board. Busy periods create scheduling queues.

evidence.note: PEC chaired by the CIO reviews new investments, dispositions and follow-ons (F2022); approval authorities set by Investment Management Authorities (F2021).

process_map.name: Obtain Board approval for large transactions and manager engagements
process_map.description: Transactions above set amounts and engagements of external managers go to the Board's Investment Strategy Committee. The board secretariat schedules the item, assembles papers and records the decision. Special meetings are called for time-critical deals.

evidence.note: Investment Strategy Committee approves certain transactions and engagement of external managers; eight regular meetings in F2022.

process_map.name: Negotiate documents and close private transactions
process_map.description: Legal counsel with external law firms negotiates purchase, shareholder, credit and fund documents, manages signing and conditions, and coordinates regulatory approvals and filings. The deal team and Tax confirm final terms. Multi-jurisdiction closings need many signatures and funds flow checks.

evidence.note: Legal support for complex deal structures described in F2022; closing count is an estimate.

process_map.name: Settle private investment cash flows at closing
process_map.description: Direct operations set up the investment in the private investments system, verify wire instructions with call-backs, obtain two authorised approvals and send payments or receive proceeds through the custodian. Records go to accounting. Wire fraud risk requires strict checks.
process_map.unit_of_work: one closing or follow-on cash flow

evidence.note: Investment closings, system set-up, transaction entries and settlements described in an investment operations posting; volume estimated.

process_map.name: Monitor and manage direct private equity portfolio companies
process_map.description: Deal teams sit on boards, review monthly and quarterly results, approve budgets and add-ons, and track value creation plans. They supply valuation inputs and propose exits. Minority positions limit control.

evidence.note: Estimate of about 150 direct and co-control companies reviewed each quarter.

process_map.name: Asset-manage real estate, infrastructure and energy holdings with partners
process_map.description: Real asset teams oversee joint ventures and platforms through boards and partner meetings, approve business plans and capital projects, and monitor operating and ESG performance. They supply valuation inputs and propose dispositions. Many assets are run by partners.

evidence.note: Estimate of about 250 assets and platforms reviewed each quarter.

process_map.name: Monitor private credit loans and process amendments and drawdowns
process_map.description: Credit staff review borrower compliance certificates and financials, track covenants and ratings, approve amendments and waivers, and request drawdowns or record repayments. Watch-list loans get restructuring plans.

evidence.note: Average credit rating B+ in F2022; loan count of about 300 is an estimate.

process_map.name: Run value creation programs with portfolio companies
process_map.description: Portfolio Value Creation works with deal teams and management to diagnose operations, agree value creation plans and run digital and data projects in material direct investments. Results feed board reviews.

evidence.note: PVC supports asset management initiatives across the global portfolio of material direct equity investments (F2021).

process_map.name: Plan and execute private equity exits
process_map.description: Deal teams decide when to sell or list a company with partners, run or join a sale process with advisors and bring the exit memo to committee. Proceeds are settled through operations. Market windows drive timing.

evidence.note: GlobalLogic sale (F2021) is an example; exit count estimated.

process_map.name: Plan and execute real asset dispositions
process_map.description: Real asset teams review holdings for sale and capital recycling, agree with partners, run sales and bring disposition memos to committee. Joint venture terms constrain timing.

evidence.note: RE actively assesses investments for disposition and recycling of capital (F2021).

process_map.name: Value private investments each quarter
process_map.description: Deal teams propose quarter-end values with models and comparables; the independent valuation group challenges them, engages third-party appraisers for the most subjective assets and loads GP net asset values for funds. The Valuation Committee approves results. Late GP reports and judgment-heavy assets slow the close.

evidence.note: Finance oversees valuation independently, uses third-party appraisers on a risk basis, Valuation Committee governance; GIPS requires quarterly private valuations.

process_map.name: Select private funds and commit capital
process_map.description: Fund teams meet general partners, review track records and terms using the ILPA questionnaire, run operational due diligence with Investment Operations, and write a commitment memo. Legal negotiates the partnership agreement and side letter. Popular funds close quickly, so decisions are rushed.

evidence.note: ILPA due diligence questionnaire and reporting templates; PE relationships with 160 fund managers.

process_map.name: Buy and sell fund interests on the secondary market
process_map.description: The secondaries team prices portfolios of LP interests and GP-led deals using fund-level data, bids through advisors and brings memos to committee. Transfers need general partner consent.

evidence.note: F&S commits to LP interests through primary and secondary markets (F2021).

process_map.name: Evaluate co-investments offered by fund partners
process_map.description: General partners offer minority co-investments alongside their funds. The team checks the deal and partner, does focused diligence and brings a memo to committee, often within two to three weeks.

evidence.note: F&S makes minority passive direct investments up to C$100 million alongside fund partners (F2021).

process_map.name: Process capital calls from general partners
process_map.description: Funds operations staff receive call notices, check amounts against commitment, fees and prior calls, verify wire instructions, obtain approvals and pay through the custodian before the due date. Records go to accounting and liquidity. Inconsistent notice formats slow review.

evidence.note: ILPA notice content and LP processing; capital calls handled by the funds operations team.

process_map.name: Process distributions from funds and partnerships
process_map.description: Staff match distribution notices to cash received at the custodian, split proceeds into return of capital, gains, income and fees, and record them. Unexplained receipts are chased with the general partner.

evidence.note: ILPA notice best practices describe distribution notice content.

process_map.name: Monitor fund investments and general partner reporting
process_map.description: Fund teams and operations review quarterly reports and capital account statements, track performance against expectations, attend annual meetings and advisory committees, and recommend re-ups. Reports arrive up to 90 days after quarter end.

evidence.note: ILPA Reporting and Performance templates; about 700 fund interests is an estimate.

process_map.name: Calculate, review and pay external management and performance fees
process_map.description: Funds operations recalculate management and performance fees from agreements and reports, compare them with manager invoices and GP statements, resolve differences and arrange payment. Fees are large and terms vary by manager.

evidence.note: Management fees C$1,294 million and performance fees C$2,386 million in F2022; fee accruals are a funds operations duty.

process_map.name: Select external managers and negotiate mandates
process_map.description: External Portfolio Management screens managers, runs investment and operational diligence with Investment Operations, Risk, Legal and Compliance, and negotiates fee terms aligned with performance. Engagements need committee and Board approval.

evidence.note: Written mandates and fee structures for external managers (F2021); Board committee approves manager engagements (F2022).

process_map.name: Process subscriptions and redemptions with external funds
process_map.description: Operations staff complete subscription documents, wire subscriptions, submit redemption notices before notice deadlines and record units and cash. Notice periods and gates make timing matter.

evidence.note: Redemptions and closings for External Portfolio Management handled by External Funds Operations.

process_map.name: Monitor external managers' performance and risk
process_map.description: EPM reviews monthly manager returns, exposures and risk reports, holds manager meetings and decides on additions, reductions or redemptions. Risk checks exposure overlap with internal programs.

evidence.note: More than 60 asset managers (F2021).

process_map.name: Measure market, credit and leverage risk and monitor limits
process_map.description: Risk runs daily and monthly potential loss, leverage, credit and liquidity measures, compares them with Board and management limits cascaded to departments, and publishes risk reports. Data gaps from private holdings require proxies.

evidence.note: Board limits cascaded to department-level limits (F2021); one-year potential loss C$97 billion (F2022).

process_map.name: Escalate and resolve risk limit breaches
process_map.description: When a limit or threshold is exceeded, Risk notifies the accountable department head and CIO, agrees a remediation plan and deadline, tracks it and reports to the Investment Risk Committee and Board where required.

evidence.note: IRC monitors risk exposures and limits; breach count is an estimate.

process_map.name: Run stress tests and scenario analysis
process_map.description: Risk runs historical and hypothetical scenarios, including inflation, geopolitical and climate scenarios, estimates fund losses and liquidity effects and reports to management and the Board.

evidence.note: Ad hoc stress scenarios such as inflation and the invasion of Ukraine, and climate scenario analysis (F2022).

process_map.name: Assess counterparty credit exposure and set limits
process_map.description: Credit risk analysts review counterparty financials and ratings, set exposure limits, monitor daily exposure after collateral and approve new counterparties before Legal signs trading agreements. Rating downgrades and market stress trigger unscheduled reviews and can force exposure cuts.

evidence.note: Counterparty credit risk named in F2022 risk sections; review count estimated.

process_map.name: Record operational incidents and assess operational risk
process_map.description: Operational risk staff log incidents from operations and technology, analyse causes, track fixes and run risk and control self-assessments with departments. Results go to the Operational and Legal Risk Committee.

evidence.note: Operational incidents reporting and key risk indicators reviewed (F2022).

process_map.name: Close the month and produce the fund's net asset value
process_map.description: Fund accounting closes the month: reconciles sub-ledgers, books accruals, takes month-end prices, external fund values and the latest private valuations, and produces the net asset value of the base and additional plan accounts. Late values and reconciliation breaks push the close.

evidence.note: Total fund valuation at least monthly under GIPS; separate base and additional plan accounts.

process_map.name: Calculate performance and attribution against benchmarks
process_map.description: Performance staff calculate fund, department and program returns, compare them with Reference Portfolio and program benchmarks, and attribute dollar value-added. Results feed Board reporting and incentive compensation. Private benchmarks and currency effects need care.

evidence.note: FAR recommends and measures program benchmarks and value-added targets; SimCorp performance module.

process_map.name: Prepare quarterly financial statements
process_map.description: After quarter close Finance prepares condensed financial statements and results commentary, gets CFRO and Audit Committee review, sends them to the stewards within 45 days and supports the results release.

evidence.note: Quarterly statements sent within 45 days of quarter end and made public within seven days.

process_map.name: Prepare the annual report and audited financial statements
process_map.description: Finance, Public Affairs, Talent and Legal draft the MD&A, compensation discussion, governance and audited statements; the auditor issues its opinion; directors approve and sign; the report goes to stewards within 60 days and is published.

evidence.note: Annual report due within 60 days of year end under s. 51 of the fund's governing act.

process_map.name: Support the external audit and special examination
process_map.description: Finance prepares evidence, valuation support and control documentation for the external auditor's year-end audit and interim reviews, and supports the special examination at least every six years.

evidence.note: Deloitte LLP audited the statements and completed the special examination in February 2022; special examination at least every six years.

process_map.name: Prepare Board and committee meeting packages
process_map.description: The board secretariat collects risk, performance, financial, audit, plan and compensation papers from owners, checks them, publishes packages on the board portal and records minutes and actions. Eight Board and 28 committee meetings a year create a steady cycle.

evidence.note: Eight Board, five Audit, five HRCC, five Governance, five Risk and eight Investment Strategy Committee meetings in F2022.

process_map.name: Communicate quarterly and annual results
process_map.description: Communications and investor relations draft news releases, presentations and media material on results, the CEO and CFRO brief media, and releases are published. Messages must match the financial statements.

evidence.note: Quarterly and annual statements must be made public.

process_map.name: Report to government stewards and hold public meetings
process_map.description: Stakeholder relations brief federal and provincial finance officials, deliver statutory reports and organise public meetings every two years in each participating province with notice published at least 10 days ahead.
process_map.unit_of_work: one stewardship briefing or public meeting

evidence.note: Public meeting every two years in each participating province with 10 days' notice (s. 52).

process_map.name: Prepare and file tax returns in foreign jurisdictions
process_map.description: Tax staff gather income and withholding data for holding entities and investments, work with local advisors to prepare returns and reclaims, file them and book tax accruals. Deadlines differ by country.

evidence.note: Taxes on income from outside Canada and indirect taxes of C$292 million in F2022.

process_map.name: Make regulatory and ownership filings in foreign jurisdictions
process_map.description: Compliance monitors holdings against ownership, short position and registration thresholds in each market, prepares filings with Legal and submits them on time. Thresholds and aggregation rules differ by country.

evidence.note: Risk-based compliance program to adhere to laws worldwide (F2022); filing count estimated.

process_map.name: Run the Investment Strategy and Risk Committee and management committees
process_map.description: The CEO chairs the ISRC of the Senior Management Team, supported by subcommittees chaired by the CIO, CFRO and General Counsel. Papers come from departments and Risk; decisions go to portfolio design and planning.

evidence.note: ISRC and subcommittees PEC, PSC, IRC and OLRC described in F2021 and F2022.

process_map.name: Develop enterprise strategy and track initiatives
process_map.description: Enterprise strategy staff refresh the multi-year strategy, set initiative milestones with department heads and report progress to the Senior Management Team each quarter. Initiatives compete with daily investing work for the same people, so milestones slip.

evidence.note: 2025 strategy described in F2021.

process_map.name: Research long-term investment strategy and beliefs
process_map.description: The Chief Investment Strategist's team researches long-horizon themes, investment beliefs and total portfolio questions, debates them with TFM and department heads, and publishes notes that inform portfolio design and management committees.

evidence.note: Chief Investment Strategist role on the Senior Management Team; output count estimated.

process_map.name: Prepare the annual business plan and operating budget
process_map.description: Planning staff collect department plans, headcount and cost requests, align them with the Strategic Portfolio and strategy, and draft the business plan and budget for the CEO and Board. Several rounds cut requests to target.

evidence.note: Business Plan with capital and operating budgets approved by the Board annually (F2022).

process_map.name: Process vendor invoices and manage operating expenses
process_map.description: Accounts payable checks invoices against contracts and budget, routes them to budget holders for approval, pays them and books expenses; analysts report spend against budget each month.

evidence.note: Operating expenses C$1,428 million (personnel C$1,013 million, general and administrative C$415 million) in F2022.

process_map.name: Run the annual performance and compensation cycle
process_map.description: Total rewards calculates incentive pools from five-year fund results and department scorecards, managers assess individuals, HR business partners calibrate, and the HRCC approves pay. Awards are loaded to payroll.

evidence.note: HRCC approves compensation structure tied to total fund, department and individual performance (F2021).

process_map.name: Recruit, hire and onboard employees
process_map.description: Recruiters open approved requisitions, source and screen candidates, run interviews with hiring managers, make offers and run background and Code of Conduct onboarding. Specialist investment roles take months to fill.

evidence.note: New recruits must agree to the Code of Conduct (F2022); hires estimated.

process_map.name: Run payroll and benefits administration
process_map.description: Payroll staff process starters, leavers and pay changes, run semi-monthly payroll, reconcile results and send payment files and ledger entries. Multi-country payroll adds local rules.

evidence.note: Estimate of semi-monthly payroll across nine offices.

process_map.name: Onboard and manage third-party vendors
process_map.description: Vendor management runs due diligence on new vendors with Information Security, Legal, Compliance and Finance, negotiates contracts and sets up the vendor for payment. Security questionnaires and contract negotiation are the slowest steps.

evidence.note: Estimate of new vendor volume for a firm with C$415 million of G&A spend.

process_map.name: Manage technology changes and releases
process_map.description: Change requests from development and data teams are risk-assessed, tested, approved at a change board and released in windows outside trading hours. Failed changes become incidents.

evidence.note: Move to nearly 100% cloud-based infrastructure (F2021); change count estimated.

process_map.name: Build and enhance investment and operations systems
process_map.description: Investment technology teams build and change trading, collateral, private markets, risk and accounting systems with business analysts and operations users, test them and release through change management. Legacy interfaces between systems make changes risky.

evidence.note: Multi-year initiative to modernise public markets trading and collateral technology (F2021).

process_map.name: Operate the enterprise data platform and data feeds
process_map.description: Data engineers ingest vendor and internal data into the cloud platform, monitor feed quality, publish curated data and onboard new datasets for investment and analytics teams.
process_map.unit_of_work: one data feed onboarded or changed

evidence.note: Cloud-based data ecosystem for data ingestion, governance and quality (F2021).

process_map.name: Maintain investment reference data and the security master
process_map.description: Data operations staff set up new securities, counterparties, accounts and standing settlement instructions, fix data exceptions flagged by downstream teams and keep reference data consistent across the order, accounting and risk systems.
process_map.unit_of_work: one reference data request or exception

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Manage user access and security monitoring
process_map.description: Security staff grant and remove system access for starters, movers and leavers after manager approval, run periodic access recertifications with system owners and monitor threats, escalating incidents to operational risk.

evidence.note: Enhanced threat detection and controls (F2021); volume estimated.

process_map.name: Resolve technology incidents and service requests
process_map.description: The service desk logs incidents and requests, resolves common issues and routes the rest to engineering. Problems that need code or configuration changes become change requests.

evidence.note: Estimate.

process_map.name: Run Code of Conduct training and compliance attestations
process_map.description: Every six months Compliance asks each director and employee to reconfirm compliance with the Code of Conduct and complete an online module, chases late responses and reports results to the Governance Committee.

evidence.note: Semiannual reconfirmation and online module for all employees (F2022); 2,052 employees times two a year.

process_map.name: Pre-clear employees' personal trades
process_map.description: Employees submit trade requests in the compliance system, which checks the restricted list and holding rules; compliance officers review exceptions and approve or deny. Records feed attestations.

evidence.note: Strict pre-clearance procedures and restrictions on personal trading (F2022).

process_map.name: Plan and perform internal audit engagements
process_map.description: Assurance and Advisory builds a risk-based annual plan approved by the Audit Committee, tests controls in each engagement, agrees findings with management and tracks remediation.

evidence.note: Assurance & Advisory is the third line; annual audit plans approved by the Audit Committee.

process_map.name: Run international office operations and local governance
process_map.description: Office leads manage premises, local licences and registrations, local entity governance and office budgets for eight offices outside Toronto, working with Legal, Compliance and Finance. Each country has its own filing and employment rules.

evidence.note: Nine global offices and 486 employees in international offices (F2021).

assumptions: The snapshot is fiscal 2022 (April 2021 to March 2022) at the end of the 2019 to 2022 reference period; headcounts, costs and the committee structure (ISRC with Portfolio Execution, Portfolio Strategy, Investment Risk and Operational and Legal Risk committees) are taken from the F2022 annual report, and department groups mostly from the F2021 report because the F2022 report does not list groups.

Investment department headcounts (TFM 80, CMF 158, AE 137, CI 137, PE 166, RA 252) are stated; all corporate function headcounts and every split below department level are estimates that make units add to 2,052 employees.

Investment operations is modelled as its own shared service reporting to the CFRO. Its teams come from job postings after 2022 and its reporting line in 2019 to 2022 is not published; it may have sat with technology or finance.

Valuations sit in Finance (independent review) and pricing and daily valuation inputs in Investment Operations, following the annual report statement that Finance oversees valuations independently of investment departments.

Treasury activities are split as described in the F2021 report: liquidity, leverage and collateral optimisation in TFM; funding, term debt and commercial paper in CMF Financing, Collateral and Trading; margin call processing in Investment Operations.
The Sustainable Investing group is placed in Real Assets because the 2022 Report on Sustainable Investing says so; in F2021 it was in Active Equities.

Loaded cost per hour = estimated total compensation (base, incentive, benefits) by level, scaled so that role headcounts times pay equal F2022 personnel expenses of C$1,013 million, times an overhead factor of 1.25 for premises, technology seats and travel, divided by 1,950 paid hours. The resulting averages are far above Job Bank market medians because incentive pay is a large share at this employer.
Public market volumes (about 25,000 orders and 48,000 settlements a month) are estimates; the organisation does not publish trade counts.

Private deal volumes are derived from an assumed 20 closings a month and the published private equity deal funnel (6.1% close rate, 23.7% reach deep diligence) and applied to PE, RA, CI and AE relationship investing alike.
Fund cash flow volumes assume about 800 fund and co-investment interests issuing four to eight notices a year each.
Quarterly processes list average monthly cases; in practice valuation and GP monitoring work is concentrated in the six weeks after quarter end, and proxy voting peaks in April to June.

Vendor names for the order management, collateral, risk, private markets and HR systems are not public and are named generically; SimCorp Dimension as the investment book of record is sourced to 2010 and to later job postings.
Board members, the external auditor and other outside bodies are external parties, not roles; the CEO's reports_to is null because the CEO reports to the Board.
